title: has anyone actually used ai tools for intraday trading?
author: chaii_biscuit
selftext:
seeing a lot of ai-based trading tools these days that claim to help with stock selection, market analysis, entry and exit signals, backtesting and even automated execution.

has anyone here actually used any such tool for intraday trading in the indian market? did it genuinely improve your decision-making, or was it mostly marketing and random signals?

not looking for guaranteed profits or paid promotions. just want to know which tools are genuinely useful, how you use them and what your experience has been.

would especially appreciate recommendations from people trading in equity intraday or f&o.

comments.author: Awkward_Weather5721
comments.body: if u want for research and backtest analysis, i would look into how finny works, [https://finnyai.tech](https://finnyai.tech), there oss trading tool is really unique and creates a validation loop that catches hallucination made by ai. BTW this is not mine, i just really love using their cli

comments.author: topsy_here
comments.body:
Yes ofcourse.

They are great at technical analysis.

If you don’t have algorithms for it yet. They know it right off the bat.

They’re also good at reasoning. So with a clever prompt they can help guide you

replies.author: Vegetable-Rub-8241
replies.body: I am developing lagias, which gives your Claude code agents the harness to use quant trading knowledge and use our alpha factors. Are still in research and just launched private waitlist. Would be nice to have you as an tester:)

comments.author: zurichbtc
comments.body: which ones have you come across so far?

comments.author: Icy_Abbreviations167
comments.body: Useful for screening news, summarizing filings and testing ideas faster. I wouldnt trust any ai generated entry or exit signal without backtesting it myself though. Most of these tools save research time, they dont magically create an edge.

comments.author: OwlZealousideal4779
comments.body:
I've been seeing tools like Alphio AI discussed for AI-assisted market analysis. I think the key question is whether they actually help traders analyze information better rather than just generate more signals.

Has anyone compared these tools with their own analysis for intraday trading? What was your experience?

comments.author: fomoz
comments.body:
I use my tool. It is free and you can run it for free. You can check my posts.

Not Indian market though, but you can trade stocks.

comments.author: Safe_Calligrapher178
comments.body: AI can be useful for research and spotting patterns, but results will vary and signals shouldn't be treated as guarantees. Prospero is one option for market research and insights, alongside independent analysis

comments.author: gray-lantern
comments.body:
Imo signal services are mostly noise.  
I think a trading AI assistant has the right to exist, but as for the rest, I’m not so sure.

comments.author: Global_Bottle3744
comments.body: I think AI is more useful after a trade than during it. It can analyze trading journals, identify patterns across similar losses, and spot where a trader broke their own rules. Markets move too fast for me to trust AI with entry and exit signals.

comments.author: LowRevolutionary539
comments.body:
I suppose yeah 
I tried it and it gave me a broader thinking on what to and what to not 
Like chart analysis and basic summarisation of everything gives an advantage
